claim_boundary.supports: Kernel-checked over any ring and any modules, degree by degree (so for complexes of any size): if linear maps rU, rM, rL commute with the boundary and differential and rM . iM = id on the middle module, a class that is not a boundary in C stays a non-boundary in D (cannot_kill), and the induced map on homology (cycles modulo boundaries, a Mathlib quotient) is injective (Hmap_injective, kernel_trivial). The two named non-examples are built in Lean as concrete degree fragments over any ring (two isolated points in an edge, degree 0; a triangle boundary in the filled triangle, degree 1), the inclusion is proved to be a chain map, the killed class is exhibited as a nonzero element of Hom sent to zero by Hmap (nontrivial ring), and no linear rU, rM, rL satisfying the chain-map and section conditions exists (no_retraction_of_killed, TwoPoints.no_chain_retraction, Triangle.no_chain_retraction); other degrees of those complexes are not formalised in Lean and retractions are required to be linear there. The converse fails over the integers in the labelled one-term instance x -> 2x (TimesTwo.converse_fails_over_int, stated through Hmap; not a subcomplex inclusion). Native over Q: 13 finite free complexes (edges, triangles, tetrahedron skeleta) with exact Betti numbers, rank of the induced homology map, killed-class counts and the rank/augmented rank of the retraction system, with an explicit verified retraction wherever one exists; one refused non-subcomplex.
claim_boundary.does_not_support: The bridge from declared inclusions to WDP-CH04-N02 (growth of the Genesis/WDP complexes does not repair an obstruction) for any actual Genesis/WDP complex pair; coefficient rings other than the declared one in the native tables; infinite or non-free complexes in the native tables; non-linear retractions and the full-complex (all degrees at once) formalisation of the two named cases; an integral failure of the converse for a genuine subcomplex inclusion (the Z instance is a one-term map, not a subcomplex); the converse over Q as a Lean theorem (it is a standard fact over a field, only observed here on the listed complexes); any physical reading.
claim_boundary.narrowest_claim: For chain maps i: C -> D and r: D -> C over a ring with r . i = id on the middle module and r commuting with the boundary, the induced map on homology is injective, so an extension admitting such an r cannot kill an old class; the two-points and triangle-with-face extensions kill a class (kernel, in the modelled degree fragment, and native) and admit no linear chain retraction (kernel, same fragment).
claim_boundary.next_test: Take one actual Genesis/WDP growth inclusion named by WDP-CH04-N02, write it in the native complex encoding with its basis subset, and decide by the retraction system and the rank of H(i) whether the old obstruction class is killed or a chain retraction exists, so that the bridge from the general theorem to the WDP growth statement is tested on a real complex.

earlier_pass.notes: Statement fidelity (lean4/ChainRetraction.lean; p2 log: cannot_kill no axioms, Hmap_injective/kernel_trivial propext+Classical.choice+Quot.sound): the two general anchors are correct and say what is claimed. cannot_kill is the elementwise form (r.i = id on the middle module, r.bd' = bd.rU, a nonboundary stays a nonboundary); Hom is cycles modulo boundaries as a Mathlib quotient and Hmap_injective builds a left inverse Hmap r from Hmap i, using only the section law and the chain-map conditions for r, so it holds degree by degree for any ring and any modules (universe 0 only). Weaker than described: (1) two_points_no_retraction and triangle_no_retraction are not statements about chain complexes. They quantify over an arbitrary function rM : (Fin n -> R) -> (Fin n -> R) with hypotheses 'rM = id' and 'rM(edgeBd e) = 0' (resp. faceBd). The reduction from 'a chain retraction of the inclusion exists' to these two hypotheses (i_0 = id so the section law forces r_0 = id; C_1 = 0 so the chain-map condition forces r_0 . bd' = 0) is done by hand in the docstring and is not kernel-checked: there is no Complex/ChainMap structure in the Lean file, no instantiation of Hmap for the two inclusions, and the sign convention of faceBd = (f, f, f) differs from the native d_2 column (1, 1, -1) (they agree only up to a sign change of a basis vector). So 'admit no retraction at all, for arbitrary functions, over every nontrivial ring' is true of the encoded system, with the encoding trusted. (2) The profile's review text calls the source theorems vacuous and these 'genuine non-existence theorems'. Having read Paper001.lean lines 453-495, the source hypotheses hfix (r0 (-1,1) = (-1,1)) and hchain (r0 (-1,1) = (0,0)) are exactly the instances of the section law and chain condition at one point; the new theorems are the universally quantified version of the same argument. That is a real but modest generalisation (arbitrary r, any nontrivial ring), not a change from vacuous to genuine; the 'vacuous' wording should be dropped from reviewed_target_qualification. (3) triangle_cycle_is_cycle is `decide` on the literal ((-1)+1, 1-1, 1-1) = (0,0,0); it mentions neither faceBd nor any boundary map, so it does not establish that the killed class is a cycle of the triangle boundary complex. It is decorative and should not be an anchor in a supports sentence. (4) converse_fails_over_int is about the linear map x -> x + x on Z having no left inverse; it is not stated with Hmap, so 'H(i) injective but no retraction' needs the hand reduction (one-term complex with zero differential, H(i) = i). It is also not an inclusion of a subcomplex, so it does not show the converse fails for extensions of the native kind over Z (an honest example of that kind would be a circle in a Moebius band; none is given). Overclaim: narrowest_claim's last clause 'the two-points and triangle-with-face extensions kill a class and therefore admit no retraction' mixes the native killed-class count with the Lean non-existence; the Lean proof does not go via cannot_kill. does_not_support says the converse over Q is 'only observed, not proved' and 'not claimed over a field': conservative and fine, but note that over a field the converse for inclusions is in fact a short theorem (degreewise split extension; zero connecting map makes the extension class null-homotopic, giving a chain retraction), so the enforcement h_injective == retraction_exists in the checker is theorem-backed, not a gamble. Checker: independent in method (rank of H(i) from rank d^D - rank(rows outside C) - rank d^C via matrix ranks only, versus the producer nullspace; retraction system via linear forms and forward elimination versus per-entry RREF; direct verification r.i = id and d^C r = r d^D). I checked the chain-map equation direction and the kernel formula: both correct (B_D intersect C_k has dimension rank d^D - rank of the rows outside C, and B_C lies inside it). It checks d^2 = 0 on every input and closedness for subcomplex status. Weak spots: free complexes over Q with an explicit chosen basis only; the canonical retraction (free unknowns 0) is compared as exact strings, which is safe only because the pivot columns coincide in both solvers; thirteen small cases, no torsion. Mutants: isolated_points_retract, triangle_class_survives_the_face, hollow_tetrahedron_class_survives and skeleton_inclusion_retracts are genuine wrong-instance near misses. non_subcomplex_gets_homology (hypothesis dropped) is good. retraction_that_is_not_a_section flips one matrix entry, a weaker check. injective_but_no_retraction's rationale is confusing (it sets retraction_exists false where H(i) is injective; it tests the converse enforcement, not a bridge). Missing: a 'retraction' that satisfies r.i = id but violates boundary commutation (on two_isolated_points_in_edge the only section-law map r_0 = id is not a chain map; a certificate claiming a retraction with r_0 = id is the exact near miss behind the node); an H(i) injective in degree 0 but killed in a higher degree only; the Z converse (needs integer data; the schema is Q). next_test: it is an own obligation (Z converse by Smith form) but a tangent: the node's declared bottleneck is the bridge to WDP-CH04-N02 ('growth does not repair'), which is only listed in does_not_support. A more pertinent next test is to introduce a Complex/ChainMap structure in Lean and derive the two named cases through Hmap_injective/cannot_kill (removing the hand reduction), then instantiate on an actual Genesis/WDP complex pair. DAG: PG-CHAIN-RETRACTION is PROVED_LEAN; the general theorem was already proved in source (Paper.lean chain_retraction_cannot_kill, Homology.lean, Paper001.lean) and the 'Instances' sentence rests on source theorems whose hypotheses are the two pointwise evaluations. The result confirms the general statement over any ring and gives instance non-existence for arbitrary functions under a hand reduction; status stands but the instance clause deserves a caveat.
